key_insight: ISLA builds physical invariances into a transformer using coordinate-free features and measure-weighted boundary attention for steady, boundary-driven PDEs.
engineering_relevance: The design targets reliable flow surrogates across object poses, unit choices, and boundary meshes, avoiding sensitivity to how the same physical problem is represented.
method: Use distances and relative angles to learned slice anchors; no learned operation receives coordinates directly.
Weight boundary sums by quadrature and normalize lengths using a boundary-derived unit.
Predict interior fields with independent queries through a tree-accelerated learned boundary kernel.
evidence_signal: On AeroZoo’s 2,816 flows, mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors are at least 3.1× and 3.3× lower than any baseline’s; on AirfRANS, ISLA ranks behind GLOBE but achieves at least 1.6× lower errors than Transolver and GeoTransolver.
watch_item: Exact equivariance and mesh-refinement consistency are stated for the every-boundary-cell-token, exact-boundary-read configuration; approximations require validation.
paper_title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs
